elements.element: Preferred: no non-solicitation obligation binding on Customer/Licensee
elements.evidence: "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party" — Licensee remains bound

elements.element: Fallback: restriction is mutual (binds both parties)
elements.evidence: "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party ... to leave his or her employment with that party"

elements.element: Fallback: limited to personnel directly involved in the services/performance
elements.evidence: "who was directly involved in the performance of this Agreement"

elements.element: Fallback: duration limited to 12 months measured from the end of that individual's involvement
elements.evidence: "During the Term of this Agreement and during the twelve (12) month period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement" — measured from Agreement end, not end of involvement
"shall not mean generally advertising job openings"
"individuals who respond to job opening advertisements or who voluntarily initiate employment inquiries"
only "solicit" is restricted; "Solicit" means "affirmative recruitment specifically aimed at one or more individuals"

reasons: The redline achieves mutuality, the directly-involved narrowing, both carve-outs and no no-hire, but the 12-month tail is measured from expiration/termination of the Agreement rather than from the end of the individual's involvement, so the restriction can run materially longer than the fallback permits for personnel who rotate off early.
Fix with a short operator change, e.g. "for twelve (12) months after that person's involvement in the performance of this Agreement ends", replacing the Term-plus-post-termination formulation.
Preferred position (no non-solicit binding Customer) is not achieved and was not the locked target; the clause still binds the Licensee, though now on a reciprocal basis.

No unrelated commercial terms were disturbed; the definition of "Solicit" and its carve-outs remain intact and the edit is confined to the operative sentence, so minimality and intent preservation hold.
